title: Exact-null dependence metrology for parallel decoders
description:
A calibrated instrument for measuring the statistical dependence a parallel or masked decoder destroys or manufactures, against nulls that are exactly zero by construction — so any dependence found off the graph was created by the system under test.

Contents:

  • Two exact nulls. A covariance-sparse ε-biased field (exact marginal independence off-graph) and a precision-sparse Gaussian Markov random field (exact conditional independence across any separator). The two fail in different places, which is the point: a scheduler can improve one while leaving the other intact or worse.
  • A continuous coupling dial with an exact feasible window ε ∈ [−1/λmax(A), +1/|λmin(A)|], both signs valid, with certified extremal values in the binary regime (odd cycles MVE(C₉) = 22/45, stars ≤ 1/√m). Ground-truth constructions built from deterministic constraints hold coupling at its maximum, which makes the question “at what coupling strength does a scheduler break?” unaskable; a continuous dial makes it measurable.
  • Per-edge hypothesis tests with false-positive control — max-statistic FWER and BH-FDR over non-edges, with calibrated p-values and calibrated intervals (plain Monte-Carlo p-values lack the resolution BH needs, and normal theory undercovers in the binary regime).
  • The ParallelBench Theorem-1 floor in closed form as comparator, plus the ideal parallel decoder as subject. For that decoder the bound is attained exactly (verified to 1.8e-15), so bound slack is zero and any gap a real model shows is entirely the model's own.
  • The nominal-token adaptation for vector-quantized image tokens: codebook projection plus the closed-form Hermite-spectrum edge target corr_proj(ρ) = Σ wk ρk. Two results generalize to any token space — the exact off-graph null survives any per-position projection by construction, while the edge target does not and must be recomputed, since |corr_proj| ≤ |ρ| means a token space strictly attenuates the dial.

Archived calibration. GATE GM1 (core, 2026-07-26): edge-CI coverage 0.948–0.951 across four zoo instances including the binary cycle at its certified extremal ε, FWER 0.025–0.060, injected-leakage power 0→1 monotone and localized at off-target FPR ≤ 8e-4, AR(1) ρd recovery 12/12, separator test nominal on the GMRF where the null is true (0.061) and firing at 1.000 on the EBF where it is false. GATE GM1-VQ (aMUSEd-256 image-VQ token space, 2026-07-27): coverage 0.948–0.951 over path/skip/grid/star graphs, FWER 0.015–0.065, power 0→1 at FPR ≤ 7e-4, AR(1) 12/12 against the projected target, separator 0.050/0.061 with the EBF arm at 1.000. Both gates are seeded and reproduce their archived reports bit-identically on the reference environment; reproduce.sh checks this and fails if any number moved.

Where the gates apply. Exact nulls require a known graph, so they exist only in the controlled setting; a real generative model has no ground-truth structure to test against, and the estimators run there with ordinary permutation nulls and known-structure probes, which these gates do not certify. Each token space needs its own pass: image VQ is cleared here, video VQ is not. Codebook resolution decides whether the conditional null exists at all — binarizing destroys it (median |partial corr| 0.0696) while full codebook resolution rescues it (0.0081).
